newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end shortened day mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end shortened day mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended an abbreviated session mostly lower, with mark and Swiss francs managing to set fresh contract lows ahead of a three-day weekend.
The currency futures pits closed at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and will be shut all day Monday in observance of Martin Luther King day in the U.S.

The shortened session did not stop dollar bulls from pushing the dollar to fresh highs of 1.6148 marks, and knocking March marks to the dollar-high equivalent of $0.6215 and the March Swiss franc contract to $0.7201.
Both of those contract lows are also close to channel lines on the charts at $0.6202 and $0.7170, respectively.
Traders anticipate short profit-taking once the contracts test those levels.
Despite the mark's sharp decline, traders reported that two firms bought a total of 10,000 March marks. The bulk of the trades were transacted between $0.6230 and $0.6237.
A total of 31,000 mark contracts traded on Friday's shortened session.
One major institution sold 2,000 March marks at $0.6233.
Marks and Swiss francs are expected to fall further, as the U.S. dollar staged an impressive rally and closed above a key retracement level of 1.6060 spot.
The 1.6060 spot level is roughly equivalent to $0.6248 in the March mark contract.
"A close above 1.6060 is a very powerful signal that the dollar is going higher," one cash dealer said.

The U.S. dollar's technical rally was sparked by several U.S. economic reports underscoring the strength of the U.S. economy. The overall U.S. trade gap grew to $8.4 billion for November, smaller than estimates for $9.8 billion.
In addition, the U.S.'s deficit with Japan fell by nearly 13 percent.

While the trade data suggested that the U.S. was importing fewer foreign goods, the gains in industrial production and capacity utilization figures for December pointed to continued activity in the U.S. manufacturing sector, analysts said.

Canadian dollar futures also closed higher, with March rising to $0.7505, near the seven-week high of $0.7507. Major resistance for March Canadian dollars is seen at $0.7510, or 1.3365 spot, and critical resistance was pegged at $0.7525, or 1.3339 spot.
In the closing minutes, a Japanese-based firm bought 370 March Canadian dollars at $0.7498 to $0.7499.

At the end of pit trade, March yen was down $0.000049 at $0.008611, marks were down $0.0074 at $0.6223, Swiss francs were $0.0101 lower at $0.7212, sterling was off $0.0076 at $1.6692, Canadian dollars were up $0.0007 at $0.7498, Australian dollars were up $0.0016 at $0.7802, and Mexican pesos were up $0.000225 at $0.124050.
